# Compiler releases

The `Release compiler` workflow creates compiler release drafts. The `Update Homebrew tap` workflow reacts when you publish a compiler release.

## One-time setup

1. Open the Matcha repository Actions settings.
2. Grant workflows read and write access to repository contents.
3. Make sure the release workflow can push its release commit to `main`.
4. Create a fine-grained personal access token for `mario-nowak/homebrew-tap`.
5. Grant the token read and write access to repository contents and pull requests.
6. Save the token as the Matcha repository Actions secret `HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN`.

## Pull request rehearsal

Every pull request runs the release workflow without remote changes. Normal CI owns compiler and end-to-end tests.

The rehearsal:

1. Updates all compiler version locations with a temporary semantic version.
2. Builds optimized Linux x86_64 and macOS arm64 binaries.
3. Confirms each binary reports the temporary version.
4. Creates and checks both release archives.
5. Generates `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
6. Updates a temporary copy of the current Homebrew formula.
7. Runs Ruby and Homebrew formula checks.

The rehearsal does not create commits, tags, releases, branches, or pull requests.

## Create a compiler release draft

1. Open [Release compiler](https://github.com/mario-nowak/matcha/actions/workflows/release-compiler.yml) in GitHub Actions.
2. Select **Run workflow**.
3. Select the `main` branch.
4. Enter a semantic version without a leading `v`, such as `0.1.2`.
5. Enable `dry_run` when you only want to rehearse the release.
6. Start the workflow.

A non-dry release runs full compiler verification before remote changes. It then:

1. Updates `matcha-compiler/build.zig`, `matcha-compiler/build.zig.zon`, and `matcha-compiler/README.md`.
2. Creates the release commit, such as `Prepare v0.1.2 release`.
3. Atomically pushes `main` and tag `matcha-compiler-v0.1.2`.
4. Creates a draft prerelease containing Linux and macOS archives with `SHA256SUMS.txt`.

The workflow safely resumes matching draft releases and tags. It rejects conflicting release state.

## Publish the compiler release

1. Open the draft on the GitHub Releases page.
2. Review the generated notes and three release assets.
3. Keep the release marked as a prerelease.
4. Select **Publish release**.

Publishing triggers the `Update Homebrew tap` workflow. That workflow validates the published release, updates `Formula/matcha-lang.rb`, and opens or reuses the tap pull request.

If the tap workflow fails, rerun it from its existing workflow run. You can also run `Update Homebrew tap` manually with the published compiler tag.

## Confirm the Homebrew update

After the tap pull request merges, run:

```sh
brew update
brew upgrade matcha-lang
matcha --version
```
